requirements.evidence: app/Ops/DiscordOpsAlert.php:82 matches the contract signature; blank() no-op at :86-88 handles null and ''; Http::timeout(5)->post($webhookUrl, ['content' => ...]) at :95; key=value lines plus mb_substr(..., 0, 1800) at :116-122; case-insensitive key-fragment redaction at :175-186, Bearer regex at :188-191, recursive redactArray + json_encode at :134-139/:156-173; non-2xx and Throwable both go to Log::error with the URL scrubbed at :99-108. config/logging.php:210 sets the LOG_STACK default to 'daily'; audit channel at :218-224 (daily, audit.log, level info, days 90); no discord channel; config/services.php:237-239; .env.example:10-18; phpunit.xml:401. The daily channel is not touched, so the test at tests/Feature/Ops/LoggingChannelsTest.php:543-549 relies on the existing LOG_DAILY_DAYS default of 14, which is fine.

conventions.evidence: Ships with Pest tests (tests/Feature/Ops/*); updates CHANGELOG.md under [Unreleased] (:31-32) and adds docs/ops/logging.md, which conventions.md already references, plus a link from docs/ops/devops.md:250; PHPDoc on the public send() at :79-81. The task explicitly requires the service class, so the 'no service layer' rule does not apply. No Livewire/UI involved.

security.evidence: Webhook URL is scrubbed from exception messages (scrub() at :196-199). The non-2xx log context only contains the status (:100-102). Sensitive keys and Bearer strings are redacted at the top level and recursively. Failures inside content() (for example an object without __toString) are also caught by the try at :92, so the caller is never broken. No weakness found.

tests.evidence: tests/Feature/Ops/DiscordOpsAlertTest.php covers the null/empty no-op (:423-434), the exact URL/method/body (:436-451), multibyte truncation to exactly 1800 (:453-461), redaction including mixed-case key, Bearer, nested JSON and a readable value (:463-502), and non-2xx plus transport-exception logging without the token (:504-532). LoggingChannelsTest covers the config contract. Weak spots: 'the audit channel accepts writes' only asserts expect(true) (:568-572) and writes a real file; the days assertions use toBe(90)/toBe(14) on raw env() values, which would be strings if a local .env set them, and phpunit.xml does not pin those keys.

simplicity.evidence: Direct implementation using Laravel's HTTP client, blank() and mb_substr. There is slight duplication: renderValue (:128-151) and redactArray (:156-173) repeat the sensitive-key and Bearer checks, and a single recursive helper could replace both.

readability.evidence: Small, well-named private methods (content, renderValue, redactArray, isSensitiveKey, containsBearerCredential, scrub); named constants MAX_LENGTH, TIMEOUT_SECONDS and SENSITIVE_KEY_FRAGMENTS; a clear class docblock; no dead code or debug output.

scope.evidence: Every file serves the task: notifier, config, env, phpunit pin, docs, changelog and tests. The notifier is not wired into any job or handler, which matches the out-of-scope list.

issues.explanation: The 'accepts writes' test asserts only expect(true) and writes to the real storage/logs/audit file instead of verifying the entry, for example with Log::spy or a temporary path.

toBe(14)/toBe(90) compare against raw env() values, which become the strings '14'/'90' when a local .env sets LOG_DAILY_DAYS/LOG_AUDIT_DAYS (as .env.example now does), and phpunit.xml does not pin those keys, so the test can depend on the local .env.
The redaction rules appear twice, in renderValue and redactArray; one recursive redact function followed by rendering would remove the duplication.
json_encode returns false on invalid UTF-8, which is cast to an empty string; JSON_INVALID_UTF8_SUBSTITUTE would keep the nested context readable.

review.summary: The change adds a small, soft-fail DiscordOpsAlert. It handles redaction, multibyte truncation and URL scrubbing in logs, adds the audit channel, sets the stack default to daily, adds the env and phpunit keys and the docs, and ships thorough Pest tests for every notifier requirement. All requirements and the contract are met. Only minor test weaknesses remain (a placeholder audit-write test and days assertions that can depend on the local .env) plus small duplication in the redaction logic, so I would approve with nits.
